title: Plancherel collision identity and Gauss-sum 2nd moment are ONE Parseval; N0=sum_b eta_b^r/q is a literal subset-collision count
wall: W-BGK (worst-case incomplete character sum M(n)=max_{b!=0}|eta_b| over thin dyadic mu_n = generalized-Paley non-principal eigenvalue / Paley Graph Conjecture)
evidence: Exact-arithmetic probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/C079_plancherel_collision_identity.py, prize regime ONLY (proper dyadic mu_n < F_q*, q prime =1 mod n, q~n^beta, beta 4.0-5.0, n=8/16/32/64, multiple primes per n: q in {4129,11593,32801,65537,1048609,...}). Three separable claims graded independently. (A) PROVEN/CONFIRMED — the raw-moment identity sum_{b in F_q} eta_b^r == q*N0(G,r), N0(G,r)=#{v in G^r: sum v_i=0 mod q}, holds EXACTLY (match=True) at every r=1..4 and every prize prime tested (e.g. n=8 q=11593: r=2 sum eta^2=92744=q*N0, r=4 sum eta^4=1947624=q*N0; n=16 q=65537: r=4 = 47186640=q*N0). This is the genuine F16 'raw moment law' (in-issue PR #417 SubgroupGaussSumRawMoment), and it makes N0 a literal combinatorial relation-count, NOT just a phase sum — that part of the connection is correct. The spectral-twin observation is also genuine: plancherel_collision (collision*|A|=sum_psi ||T_psi||^2) and subgroup_gaussSum_secondMoment (sum_b ||eta_b||^2=q|G|) are both instances of one orthogonality/Plancherel relation, at group levels A and F respectively — the in-tree lemmas are real and axiom-clean. (B) REFUTED — the HEADLINE 'N0 is LITERALLY MomentCollisionSpectral.collision' is false as an identity. collision(a)=#{ordered pairs of a-element SUBSETS (repetition-free within each set) of G with equal subset-sum}; N0(G,2a)=#{ordered 2a-TUPLES (repeats allowed, no subset structure) summing to 0}. They coincide only at a=1 (8=8, 16=16, both collapse to |G|) and DIVERGE for every a>=2: a=2 gives collision=40 vs N0(4)=168 (n=8), 176 vs 720 (n=16), 736 vs 2976 (n=32), 3008 vs 12096 (n=64); a=3 gives 104 vs 5120 (n=8). collision/N0 settles around 1/4.2. They are categorically different objects (subset-collision count over A=F vs additive-relation tuple count over F), exactly the C031-style conflation. (C) OPEN, welds to BGK — the actionable payoff ('port SubsetSumPaleyZygmund manyHeavyTargets to the eta side: small eta-collision 2nd moment => many heavy frequencies, a new anti-concentration constraint attacking F2') produces a LOWER bound on the NUMBER of heavy frequencies (probe: PZ count-LB at t=1/2 ~ 1105/5831/90228 vs actual heavy counts 5792/32192/509024 — valid but loose lower bound), whereas the prize core needs an UPPER bound on the MAX M(n)=max_{b!=0}|eta_b|. A lower-bound-on-a-count never yields an upper-bound-on-a-max, so PZ gives NO new M(n) bound. Moreover PZ consumes only E[X]=M2/q=n (2nd moment, in tree) and E[X^2]=M4/q=E_2(G) (4th moment, in tree) — it is a re-reading of the SAME two Parseval moments, no new analytic input. The probe re-confirms the BGK wall numerically: M(n)/sqrt(n log(q/n)) ~ 0.96->1.30 (rising, matches grounding sec5), M(n) > 2sqrt(n) at every prime (non-Ramanujan, e.g. n=32 q=1048609: M(n)=22.98 vs 2sqrt(n)=11.31).
honest_note: PARTIAL (not REFUTED, not REDUCED): the raw-moment identity (A) and the two-group-levels-one-Parseval structural observation are genuinely correct and the cited in-tree lemmas (plancherel_collision, subgroup_gaussSum_secondMoment, addEnergy_le_of_charSum_bound) are real and axiom-clean; only the 'N0 is LITERALLY collision' headline (B) is false (subset-collision count != additive tuple-relation count; agree only at a=1, diverge for all a>=2) and the proposed Paley-Zygmund payoff (C) does not advance the prize. No closure of anything. The connection is an identity-plus-spectral-restatement, not a bound; its proposed new constraint (anti-concentration / many heavy frequencies) is a LOWER bound on a count, which is structurally the wrong inequality direction for the prize (which needs an UPPER bound on the worst frequency), and it reuses only the 2nd and 4th Parseval moments already in tree. It welds back to W-BGK: bounding M(n)=max_{b!=0}|eta_b| for thin dyadic mu_n = the generalized-Paley non-principal eigenvalue = the 25-year-open Paley Graph / BGK square-root-cancellation problem. Same family as C031 (CS25 2nd moment != E_2; diagonal is the FAVORABLE term) and C020 (CS25 off-diagonal = M(n) = BGK; L2 mass is free, L-inf worst frequency is the open core). Recommend a DISPROOF_LOG one-liner: 'C079: raw-moment law sum_b eta_b^r=q*N0 is genuine (F16), but N0!=collision (subset-pair vs tuple, diverge a>=2); Paley-Zygmund on {eta_b} is a LOWER bound on #heavy-frequencies (wrong direction; needs UPPER bound on max) using only the in-tree 2nd+4th moments => no new M(n) bound, welds to BGK.'
